we have proposed a novel hierarchical probabilistic framework that uses a Gabor filter bank to optimally separate the edema from tumour in brain MRIs, followed by a modified MRF model that refines the tumour and edema boundaries.
a hierarchical Gabor and MFR framework for segmentation of brain tumours (including the edema) in MRI volumes has been developed and tested on a large number of clinical cases.
a hierarchical probabilistic Gabor-MRF framework can be used to accurately segment brain tumours from MRIs, and that the proposed method outperforms the top methods on the BRATS challenge.

the development of an automated method to segment brain tumours (including the edema) in MRI volumes.
the development of novel techniques to improve the segmentation of brain tumours from MRIs, and in particular to improve the separation of the tumour core and edema.
the development and evaluation of an automated method to segment brain tumour (including the edema) from multispectral MRIs.

our method is the best performing method in the BRATS challenge for the tumour core segmentation task.
this paper presents a novel hierarchical probabilistic framework that is fully automated and robust for brain tumour segmentation in MRI.
this paper provides a novel, robust and fully automated framework for brain tumour segmentation that outperforms state of the art methods on both low and high grade brain tumours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a fully automatic, robust and fast method that is able to segment both low and high grade brain tumour cores with a Dice score of 80% and 75% respectively, and an edema volume Dice score of 65%.
the proposed method is a fully automatic method that can segment both tumour core and edema in multispectral MRIs.
we have developed a fully automated hierarchical segmentation method that can be used for the segmentation of brain tumours from MRIs in a fully automated manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a customised GMM based MRF can provide a robust framework for brain tumour segmentation, while maintaining the advantages of both the probabilistic and the MRF based frameworks.
the proposed method is fully automatic and can be applied to both low grade and high grade brain tumours with a single set of parameters.

a customised GABOR-MRF approach is able to segment brain tumours (including the edema), with a good level of performance, in a fully automated manner, with no need for user input or manual intervention, which can be used in clinical applications.
